decisions.choice: the virgin: young women as a group
decisions.reason: The word is singular, "the virgin", but here it stands for the young women of the people, set beside the young men and the old men. It is not the title "virgin Israel" of verse 4.

decisions.choice: I will turn their mourning into joy: God reverses the grief of the exile
decisions.reason: The verse answers the laments of the destruction, when joy and the sound of celebration were silenced (7:34; 16:9; 25:10). God himself makes the change (Psalm 30:12).

decisions.choice: glad from their sorrow: gladness that comes after and in place of sorrow
decisions.reason: The small word "from" can mean "after" or "instead of"; both describe sorrow giving way to joy.

decisions.choice: the young women (Balanced); the girls (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the collective singular plural.

source.text: וְרִוֵּיתִ֛י נֶ֥פֶשׁ הַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים דָּ֑שֶׁן וְעַמִּ֛י אֶת־טוּבִ֥י יִשְׂבָּ֖עוּ נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And I will saturate [the] soul of the priests [with] fatness, and my people [with] my goodness will be satisfied, declares Yahweh.

en.L: And I will saturate the soul of the priests [with] fatness, \q and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people will be satisfied with {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} goodness, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: I will fill the priests with rich food in abundance, \q and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people will have their fill of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} good gifts, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: I will give the priests more than enough of the best food, \q and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people will be filled with the good things I give them, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: Y saciaré el alma de los sacerdotes [con] abundancia, \q y {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo se saciará de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} bondad, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.B: Llenaré a los sacerdotes de comida abundante y rica, \q y {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo se saciará de {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} buenos dones, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.R: Les daré a los sacerdotes más que suficiente de la mejor comida, \q y {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo se llenará de las cosas buenas que yo le doy, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.

fr.L: Et je rassasierai l’âme des prêtres de graisse, \q et {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple sera rassasié de {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} bienfaits, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Je comblerai les prêtres de mets riches en abondance, \q et {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple sera rassasié de {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} bienfaits, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Je donnerai aux prêtres plus qu’assez de la meilleure nourriture, \q et {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple sera comblé des bonnes choses que je lui donne, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.

sw.L: Nami nitaishibisha nafsi ya makuhani [kwa] unono, \q na watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} watashiba wema {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Nitawashibisha makuhani kwa vyakula vinono tele, \q na watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} watashiba zawadi {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}} njema, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Nitawapa makuhani vyakula bora kupita kiasi, \q na watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} watashiba mambo mema ninayowapa, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

vi.L: Ta sẽ làm cho linh hồn các thầy tế lễ no nê [bằng] mỡ béo, \q và dân {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ được thỏa mãn với sự tốt lành của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy.
vi.B: Ta sẽ cho các thầy tế lễ ăn uống dư dật những món béo bổ, \q và dân {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ được no đủ với những ân phước của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy.
vi.R: Ta sẽ cho các thầy tế lễ được ăn thức ăn ngon nhất, còn dư nữa, \q và dân {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ được no nê với những điều tốt lành {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ban cho họ, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán.

ko.L: 그리고 내가 제사장들의 영혼을 기름진 것으로 흡족하게 하고, \q 내 백성은 내 좋은 것으로 배부를 것이다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 선언이다.
ko.B: 내가 제사장들에게 기름진 음식을 넉넉히 주고, \q 내 백성은 내가 베푸는 좋은 것들로 배부를 것이다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.
ko.R: 내가 제사장들에게 가장 좋은 음식을 넘치도록 주겠다. \q 내 백성은 내가 주는 좋은 것들로 배부를 것이다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.

pt.L: E saciarei a alma dos sacerdotes [com] gordura, \q e o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} povo se fartará da {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} bondade, declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}.
pt.B: Encherei os sacerdotes de comida farta, \q e o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} povo se fartará dos {{deity_pronoun:meus|Meus}} bons presentes, declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}.
pt.R: Vou dar aos sacerdotes mais do que o suficiente da melhor comida, \q e o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} povo vai ficar satisfeito com as coisas boas que eu lhe dou, diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}.

decisions.choice: fatness: the rich portions of the sacrifices that fed the priests
decisions.reason: The priests lived on their share of the offerings (Leviticus 7:31-36; Deuteronomy 18:1-3). If they have plenty, the people are bringing many sacrifices, and worship at the temple is restored.

decisions.choice: saturate the soul: satisfy the appetite fully
decisions.reason: The verb means to give plenty to drink, to drench. "Soul" here is the appetite or the person who longs to be filled (Psalm 107:9). The same verb returns in verse 25.

decisions.choice: my goodness: the good things God gives
decisions.reason: As in verse 12, "goodness" means God's gifts of food and plenty.

decisions.choice: declares the LORD (Literal, Balanced); says the LORD (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in Isaiah, each level keeps one wording for this formula.

source.text: כֹּ֣ה׀אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה ק֣וֹל בְּרָמָ֤ה נִשְׁמָע֙ נְהִי֙ בְּכִ֣י תַמְרוּרִ֔ים רָחֵ֖ל מְבַכָּ֣ה עַל־בָּנֶ֑יהָ מֵאֲנָ֛ה לְהִנָּחֵ֥ם עַל־בָּנֶ֖יהָ כִּ֥י אֵינֶֽנּוּ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Thus says Yahweh: A voice in Ramah is heard, lamentation, weeping of bitterness; Rachel weeping over her children; she refuses to be comforted over her children, because he is not.

en.L: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: A voice is heard in Ramah, lamentation [and] bitter weeping; \q Rachel is weeping over her children; \q she refuses to be comforted over her children, because they are not.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: In Ramah a voice is heard, mourning and bitter weeping: \q Rachel weeping for her children. \q She will not let anyone comfort her for her children, because they are gone.
en.R: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: People hear a sound in Ramah, the sound of crying and bitter sadness. \q Rachel is crying for her children. \q She will not let anyone comfort her, because her children are gone.

es.L: Así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: Una voz se oye en Ramá, lamento [y] llanto amargo; \q Raquel llora por sus hijos; \q no quiere ser consolada por sus hijos, porque ya no existen.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dice esto: En Ramá se oye una voz, lamento y llanto amargo: \q es Raquel que llora por sus hijos. \q No deja que nadie la consuele por sus hijos, porque ya no están.
es.R: Esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: La gente oye un sonido en Ramá, el sonido de llanto y de amarga tristeza. \q Raquel llora por sus hijos. \q No deja que nadie la consuele, porque sus hijos ya no están.

fr.L: Ainsi parle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : Une voix est entendue à Rama, une lamentation, des pleurs amers ; \q Rachel pleure ses enfants ; \q elle refuse d’être consolée au sujet de ses enfants, parce qu’ils ne sont plus.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit ceci : À Rama, on entend une voix, une lamentation et des pleurs amers : \q c’est Rachel qui pleure ses enfants. \q Elle ne veut pas qu’on la console pour ses enfants, parce qu’ils ont disparu.
fr.R: Voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : Les gens entendent un bruit à Rama, des pleurs et une tristesse amère. \q Rachel pleure ses enfants. \q Elle ne veut pas qu’on la console, parce que ses enfants ne sont plus là.

sw.L: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asema hivi: Sauti inasikika katika Rama, maombolezo [na] kilio cha uchungu; \q Raheli anawalilia watoto wake; \q anakataa kufarijiwa kwa ajili ya watoto wake, kwa sababu hawapo.
sw.B: Hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asemavyo: Katika Rama sauti inasikika, maombolezo na kilio cha uchungu: \q Raheli akiwalilia watoto wake. \q Hamwachi mtu yeyote amfariji kwa ajili ya watoto wake, kwa sababu wametoweka.
sw.R: Hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} analosema: Watu wanasikia sauti katika Rama, sauti ya kilio na huzuni kuu. \q Raheli anawalilia watoto wake. \q Hamwachi mtu yeyote amfariji, kwa sababu watoto wake wametoweka.

vi.L: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán thế này: Có tiếng được nghe tại Ra-ma, tiếng than van [và] khóc lóc đắng cay; \q Ra-chên khóc thương con cái mình; \q bà không chịu được an ủi về con cái mình, vì chúng không còn nữa.
vi.B: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán như vầy: Tại Ra-ma vang lên một tiếng, tiếng than khóc và khóc lóc đắng cay: \q Ra-chên khóc thương con cái mình. \q Bà không chịu để ai an ủi về con cái mình, vì chúng đã không còn nữa.
vi.R: Đây là lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán: Người ta nghe một tiếng ở Ra-ma, tiếng khóc than và buồn khổ đắng cay. \q Ra-chên đang khóc vì các con mình. \q Bà không muốn ai an ủi mình, vì các con bà đã không còn nữa.

ko.L: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이와 같이 말씀하신다. 라마에서 소리가 들린다. 애곡과 쓰라린 통곡이다. \q 라헬이 자기 자식들 때문에 울고 있다. \q 그가 자기 자식들 때문에 위로받기를 거절한다. 그들이 없기 때문이다.
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이렇게 말씀하신다. 라마에서 소리가 들린다. 슬피 우는 소리와 쓰라리게 통곡하는 소리다. \q 라헬이 자식들 때문에 울고 있다. \q 자식들이 없어졌으니 어떤 위로도 받지 않으려 한다.
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 하시는 말씀이다. 라마 마을에서 소리가 들린다. 울부짖으며 몹시 슬퍼하는 소리다. \q 라헬이 자기 아이들 때문에 울고 있다. \q 아이들이 사라졌으니 라헬은 아무에게서도 위로받으려 하지 않는다.

pt.L: Assim diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}: Uma voz é ouvida em Ramá, lamentação [e] choro amargo; \q Raquel chorando por seus filhos; \q ela se recusa a ser consolada por seus filhos, porque eles já não existem.
pt.B: Assim diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}: Ouve-se um som em Ramá, lamento e choro amargo: \q Raquel chora por seus filhos. \q Ela recusa todo consolo por seus filhos, porque eles se foram.
pt.R: É isto que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} diz: As pessoas ouvem um som na cidade de Ramá. É o som de choro e de tristeza amarga. \q Raquel está chorando por seus filhos. \q Ela não deixa ninguém consolá-la, porque os filhos dela se foram.

decisions.choice: Ramah: a town of Benjamin a few miles north of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Ramah lay on the road north out of Jerusalem. Jeremiah himself was set free there from among the captives being taken to Babylon (40:1), so it was a place where exiles were gathered. Rachel's tomb was remembered as being in the territory of Benjamin (1 Samuel 10:2), not far away.

decisions.choice: Rachel weeping for her children: Israel's ancestor mother grieving over her descendants taken away
decisions.reason: Rachel was Jacob's beloved wife, the mother of Joseph (father of Ephraim and Manasseh) and of Benjamin; she died giving birth to Benjamin (Genesis 35:16-20). The poem pictures her crying from her grave as her descendants, the northern tribes and Benjamin, are led into exile.

decisions.choice: because they are not: her children are gone, taken away or dead
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "because he is not", using the singular for the children as one group. "Is not" means no longer present (Genesis 37:30; 42:36). Verses 16-17 answer it: they will return.

decisions.choice: used in the New Testament: Matthew 2:18
decisions.reason: Matthew quotes this verse when Herod kills the young boys of Bethlehem, seeing in Rachel's weeping a picture of the mothers' grief (Matthew 2:16-18). In Jeremiah the lament is followed at once by the promise that her children will come home.

decisions.choice: She will not let anyone comfort her (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "refuses to be comforted" means that she turns away all comfort; Balanced and Readable say so actively.

decisions.choice: Ramá ... Raquel llora por sus hijos ... ya no existen / ya no están
decisions.reason: Matthew 2:18 quotes this verse; the key words of the published Spanish there are kept ("Ramá", "Raquel", "llora por sus hijos", "no quiere ser consolada", "ya no existen" / "ya no están"), while the rest follows the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: Rama, Raheli
decisions.reason: Matthew 2:18 quotes this verse; Swahili keeps the published names "Rama" and "Raheli" and its key words (kilio, kufarijiwa), while the wording is drafted from the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: "à Rama ... Rachel pleure ses enfants ... parce qu'ils ne sont plus"
decisions.reason: The key words of Matthew 2:18 in French, which quotes this verse, so a reader can see the quotation; the rest is drafted from the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: "Ra-ma", "Ra-chên", "không còn nữa"
decisions.reason: Matthew 2:18 quotes this verse, so the names and key words are the published ones of that verse, while the wording is drafted from the Hebrew, which has no "children" in the last clause and says only "they are not".

decisions.choice: "라마", "라헬", "위로받기를 거절하다"
decisions.reason: Matthew 2:18 quotes this verse (meaning decision m4). Korean keeps its key words (라마, 라헬, 자식들, 위로) so the quotation can be seen, but the sentences are drafted from the Hebrew, in the present tense as the Hebrew has it.

decisions.choice: Uma voz ... ouvida em Ramá; Raquel chorando por seus filhos; porque eles já não existem (L); Ouve-se um som; recusa todo consolo; porque eles se foram (B)
decisions.reason: Matthew 2:18 quotes the verse (m4), and its Portuguese is kept where the Hebrew allows. The differences: the Hebrew verb is a present ("é ouvida", "ouve-se"), where Matthew's Greek has a past; the Hebrew says "choro amargo" where Matthew has "grande lamentação" / "lamento sem fim"; and Readable says "se foram" rather than Matthew's "tinham morrido", because in Jeremiah the children are exiles who come home (verses 16-17, m3).

source.text: כֹּ֣ה׀אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה מִנְעִ֤י קוֹלֵךְ֙ מִבֶּ֔כִי וְעֵינַ֖יִךְ מִדִּמְעָ֑ה כִּי֩ יֵ֨שׁ שָׂכָ֤ר לִפְעֻלָּתֵךְ֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה וְשָׁ֖בוּ מֵאֶ֥רֶץ אוֹיֵֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus says Yahweh: Restrain your voice from weeping and your eyes from tears, for there is a reward for your work, declares Yahweh, and they will return from [the] land of [the] enemy.

en.L: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: Restrain your voice from weeping \q and your eyes from tears, \q for there is a reward for your work, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q and they will return from the land of the enemy.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: Hold back your voice from weeping \q and your eyes from tears, \q for your labor will have its reward, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; \q they will come back from the land of the enemy.
en.R: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: Stop crying. \q Wipe the tears from your eyes. \q What you have done will be rewarded, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q Your children will come back from the enemy's land.

es.L: Así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: Reprime tu voz del llanto \q y tus ojos de las lágrimas, \q porque hay recompensa para tu trabajo, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, \q y volverán de la tierra del enemigo.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dice esto: Contén tu voz del llanto \q y tus ojos de las lágrimas, \q porque tu trabajo tendrá su recompensa, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}; \q volverán de la tierra del enemigo.
es.R: Esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: Deja de llorar. \q Sécate las lágrimas de los ojos. \q Lo que has hecho será recompensado, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. \q Tus hijos volverán de la tierra del enemigo.

fr.L: Ainsi parle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : Retiens ta voix des pleurs \q et tes yeux des larmes, \q car il y a un salaire pour ta peine, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, \q et ils reviendront du pays de l’ennemi.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit ceci : Retiens tes pleurs \q et sèche les larmes de tes yeux, \q car ta peine sera récompensée, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ; \q ils reviendront du pays de l’ennemi.
fr.R: Voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : Arrête de pleurer. \q Essuie les larmes de tes yeux. \q Ce que tu as fait sera récompensé, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. \q Tes enfants reviendront du pays de l’ennemi.

sw.L: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asema hivi: Izuie sauti yako isilie, \q na macho yako yasitoe machozi, \q kwa maana kazi yako ina thawabu, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, \q nao watarudi kutoka nchi ya adui.
sw.B: Hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asemavyo: Izuie sauti yako na kilio, \q na macho yako na machozi, \q kwa maana taabu yako itapata thawabu, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}; \q watarudi kutoka nchi ya adui.
sw.R: Hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} analosema: Acha kulia. \q Futa machozi machoni pako. \q Ulichokifanya kitapata thawabu, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. \q Watoto wako watarudi kutoka nchi ya adui.

vi.L: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán thế này: Hãy nín tiếng khóc \q và giữ mắt khỏi rơi lệ, \q vì công khó của ngươi sẽ có phần thưởng, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy, \q và chúng sẽ trở về từ xứ của kẻ thù.
vi.B: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán như vầy: Hãy nín tiếng khóc \q và lau ráo nước mắt, \q vì công khó của con sẽ được đền bù, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy; \q chúng sẽ trở về từ xứ của kẻ thù.
vi.R: Đây là lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán: Đừng khóc nữa. \q Hãy lau nước mắt. \q Những điều con đã làm sẽ được đền đáp, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán. \q Con cái con sẽ trở về từ xứ của kẻ thù.

ko.L: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이와 같이 말씀하신다. 네 목소리를 그쳐 울지 말고, \q 네 눈에서 눈물을 거두어라. \q 네 수고에 보상이 있을 것이다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 선언이다. \q 그들이 원수의 땅에서 돌아올 것이다.
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이렇게 말씀하신다. 울음소리를 그치고, \q 눈에서 눈물을 거두어라. \q 네 수고가 보상을 받을 것이다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다. \q 그들이 원수의 땅에서 돌아올 것이다.
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 하시는 말씀이다. 이제 그만 울어라. \q 눈물을 닦아라. \q 네가 한 일이 보상을 받을 것이다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다. \q 네 자녀들이 원수의 땅에서 돌아올 것이다.

pt.L: Assim diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}: Contém a tua voz do choro \q e os teus olhos das lágrimas, \q pois há recompensa para o teu trabalho, declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, \q e eles voltarão da terra do inimigo.
pt.B: Assim diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}: Segura a tua voz e não chores, \q segura as lágrimas dos teus olhos, \q pois o teu trabalho terá a sua recompensa, declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}; \q eles voltarão da terra do inimigo.
pt.R: É isto que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} diz: Para de chorar. \q Enxuga as lágrimas dos teus olhos. \q O que fizeste vai ser recompensado, diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}. \q Os teus filhos vão voltar da terra do inimigo.

decisions.choice: a reward for your work: Rachel's labor as a mother will not be wasted
decisions.reason: Her work is bearing and raising children. Since her children will come back, her labor has its reward (compare Isaiah 49:4; 65:23).

decisions.choice: they will return: Rachel's children, the exiles
decisions.reason: "They" are the children she weeps for in verse 15.

decisions.choice: Your children
decisions.reason: Readable names who will return.

decisions.choice: tu (God to Rachel)
decisions.reason: God speaks to Rachel, one person, with "tu", as he speaks to one person through the book; Readable uses the "tu" imperative "Para", "Enxuga", the forms that go with it.

source.text: וְיֵשׁ־תִּקְוָ֥ה לְאַחֲרִיתֵ֖ךְ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֑ה וְשָׁ֥בוּ בָנִ֖ים לִגְבוּלָֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And there is hope for your future, declares Yahweh, and children will return to their territory.

en.L: And there is hope for your future, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q and children will return to their own territory.
en.B: There is hope for your future, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; \q your children will come back to their own land.
en.R: There is hope for you in the days ahead, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q Your children will come back to their own land.

es.L: Y hay esperanza para tu porvenir, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, \q y los hijos volverán a su territorio.
es.B: Hay esperanza para tu futuro, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}; \q tus hijos volverán a su propia tierra.
es.R: Hay esperanza para ti en los días que vienen, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. \q Tus hijos volverán a su propia tierra.

fr.L: Et il y a de l’espérance pour ton avenir, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, \q et les fils reviendront dans leur territoire.
fr.B: Il y a de l’espoir pour ton avenir, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ; \q tes enfants reviendront dans leur pays.
fr.R: Il y a de l’espoir pour toi dans les jours à venir, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. \q Tes enfants reviendront dans leur pays.

sw.L: Na kuna tumaini kwa wakati wako ujao, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, \q na watoto watarudi katika nchi yao wenyewe.
sw.B: Kuna tumaini kwa wakati wako ujao, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}; \q watoto wako watarudi katika nchi yao wenyewe.
sw.R: Kuna tumaini kwako katika siku zijazo, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. \q Watoto wako watarudi katika nchi yao wenyewe.

vi.L: Có hy vọng cho tương lai ngươi, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy, \q và con cái sẽ trở về bờ cõi của mình.
vi.B: Có hy vọng cho tương lai của con, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy; \q con cái con sẽ trở về quê hương mình.
vi.R: Những ngày sắp tới vẫn có hy vọng cho con, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán. \q Con cái con sẽ trở về quê hương mình.

ko.L: 그리고 너의 장래에 희망이 있다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 선언이다. \q 자식들이 자기들의 땅으로 돌아올 것이다.
ko.B: 너의 앞날에는 희망이 있다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다. \q 네 자녀들이 자기들의 땅으로 돌아올 것이다.
ko.R: 너에게는 앞으로 희망이 있다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다. \q 네 자녀들이 자기들의 땅으로 돌아올 것이다.

pt.L: E há esperança para o teu futuro, declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, \q e os filhos voltarão para o seu território.
pt.B: Há esperança para o teu futuro, declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}; \q os teus filhos voltarão para a sua própria terra.
pt.R: Há esperança para ti nos dias que virão, diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}. \q Os teus filhos vão voltar para a sua própria terra.

decisions.choice: your future: what lies ahead for you, including descendants
decisions.reason: The word means the end or latter part of something, and so the future (29:11). Rachel's future is her children and their children.

decisions.choice: their own territory: the land of their tribes
decisions.reason: The word means a border, and so the land within it. The exiles will go back to their own tribal land.

decisions.choice: your children
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "children"; Balanced and Readable add "your", since they are Rachel's children of verse 15.

source.text: שָׁמ֣וֹעַ שָׁמַ֗עְתִּי אֶפְרַ֨יִם֙ מִתְנוֹדֵ֔ד יִסַּרְתַּ֨נִי֙ וָֽאִוָּסֵ֔ר כְּעֵ֖גֶל לֹ֣א לֻמָּ֑ד הֲשִׁיבֵ֣נִי וְאָשׁ֔וּבָה כִּ֥י אַתָּ֖ה יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: Surely I have heard Ephraim bemoaning himself: You disciplined me, and I was disciplined, like a calf [that was] not trained; bring me back, and I will return, for you [are] Yahweh my God.

en.L: I have surely heard Ephraim grieving: \q "You disciplined me, and I was disciplined, \q like a calf not trained; \q bring me back, and I will come back, \q for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} [are] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} my God.
en.B: I have certainly heard Ephraim grieving: \q "You disciplined me, and I took the discipline, \q like a calf never trained to the yoke. \q Bring me back, and I will come back, \q for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} my God.
en.R: I have clearly heard Ephraim crying: \q "You corrected me, and I was corrected, \q like a young calf that had never been trained. \q Bring me back, and I will come back to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, \q because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} my God.

es.L: Ciertamente he oído a Efraín lamentarse: \q «Me castigaste, y fui castigado, \q como novillo no domado; \q hazme volver, y volveré, \q porque {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} [eres] {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} mi Dios.
es.B: He oído claramente a Efraín lamentarse: \q «Me corregiste, y acepté la corrección, \q como un novillo nunca acostumbrado al yugo. \q Hazme volver, y volveré, \q porque {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} eres {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} mi Dios.
es.R: He oído claramente a Efraín llorar: \q «Me corregiste, y fui corregido, \q como un ternero que nunca había sido domado. \q Hazme volver, y volveré a {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}, \q porque {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} eres {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} mi Dios.

fr.L: J’ai bien entendu Éphraïm se lamenter : \q « Tu m’as corrigé, et j’ai été corrigé, \q comme un veau non dressé ; \q fais-moi revenir, et je reviendrai, \q car {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} [es] {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} mon Dieu.
fr.B: J’ai bien entendu Éphraïm se lamenter : \q « Tu m’as corrigé, et j’ai accepté la correction, \q comme un jeune taureau jamais dressé au joug. \q Fais-moi revenir, et je reviendrai, \q car {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} es {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} mon Dieu.
fr.R: J’ai bien entendu Éphraïm pleurer : \q « Tu m’as corrigé, et j’ai été corrigé, \q comme un jeune veau qu’on n’avait jamais dressé. \q Fais-moi revenir, et je reviendrai vers {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, \q car {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} es {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} mon Dieu.

sw.L: Hakika nimemsikia Efraimu akijililia: \q "Umeniadibisha, nami nikaadibishwa, \q kama ndama asiyefundishwa; \q unirudishe, nami nitarudi, \q kwa maana {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} [ndiwe] {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wangu.
sw.B: Hakika nimemsikia Efraimu akiomboleza: \q "Uliniadibisha, nami nikaikubali adhabu, \q kama ndama ambaye hajazoezwa nira. \q Unirudishe, nami nitarudi, \q kwa maana {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ndiwe {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wangu.
sw.R: Nimemsikia wazi Efraimu akilia: \q "Ulinirekebisha, nami nikarekebishwa, \q kama ndama mchanga ambaye hajawahi kufundishwa. \q Unirudishe, nami nitarudi {{deity_pronoun:kwako|Kwako}}, \q kwa sababu {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ndiwe {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wangu.

vi.L: Ta đã nghe rõ Ép-ra-im than thở: \q "Ngài đã sửa phạt con, và con đã bị sửa phạt, \q như con bò con chưa được tập; \q xin đem con trở lại, thì con sẽ trở lại, \q vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} [là] {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của con.
vi.B: Ta đã nghe rõ Ép-ra-im than thở: \q "Ngài đã sửa phạt con, và con đã chịu sửa phạt, \q như con bò con chưa hề được tập mang ách. \q Xin đem con trở lại, thì con sẽ trở lại, \q vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của con.
vi.R: Ta đã nghe rõ Ép-ra-im khóc than: \q "Ngài đã sửa dạy con, và con đã được sửa dạy, \q như một con bò tơ chưa bao giờ được tập. \q Xin đem con trở lại, thì con sẽ trở lại cùng Ngài, \q vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của con.

ko.L: 에브라임이 탄식하는 것을 내가 분명히 들었다. \q "주님께서 저를 징계하셨고, 저는 징계를 받았습니다. \q 길들지 않은 송아지 같았습니다. \q 저를 돌이켜 주십시오. 그러면 제가 돌아가겠습니다. \q 주님은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 저의 하나님이십니다.
ko.B: 에브라임이 탄식하는 소리를 내가 분명히 들었다. \q "주님께서 저를 징계하셨고, 저는 징계를 받았습니다. \q 멍에에 길들지 않은 송아지 같았습니다. \q 저를 돌아가게 해 주십시오. 그러면 제가 돌아가겠습니다. \q 주님은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 저의 하나님이십니다.
ko.R: 에브라임이 우는 소리를 내가 똑똑히 들었다. \q "주님께서 저를 바로잡으셨고, 저는 바로잡혔습니다. \q 저는 길들지 않은 어린 송아지 같았습니다. \q 저를 돌아가게 해 주십시오. 그러면 제가 주님께 돌아가겠습니다. \q 주님은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 저의 하나님이십니다.

pt.L: Eu bem ouvi Efraim lamentando-se: \q "Tu me disciplinaste, e eu fui disciplinado, \q como um bezerro não ensinado; \q faze-me voltar, e eu voltarei, \q pois {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} [és] {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, meu Deus.
pt.B: Eu ouvi muito bem Efraim se lamentar: \q "Tu me disciplinaste, e eu aceitei a disciplina, \q como um bezerro nunca acostumado ao jugo. \q Faze-me voltar, e eu voltarei, \q pois {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} és {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, meu Deus.
pt.R: Eu ouvi claramente Efraim chorando: \q "Tu me corrigiste, e eu fui corrigido, \q como um bezerro novo que nunca tinha sido treinado. \q Traze-me de volta, e eu voltarei para {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}, \q porque {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} és {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, meu Deus.

decisions.choice: I have surely heard Ephraim: God speaks, and Ephraim's own prayer follows to the end of verse 19
decisions.reason: The doubled verb stresses that God has truly heard. Ephraim, the leading tribe of the north, stands for the northern people (verse 9). The verb for grieving means to shake the head or rock to and fro in sorrow.

decisions.choice: like a calf not trained: a young animal that resisted the yoke until it was broken in
decisions.reason: Hosea pictures Ephraim as a stubborn heifer (Hosea 4:16; 10:11). The discipline was the suffering of defeat and exile; Ephraim now accepts that it was needed.

decisions.choice: bring me back, and I will come back: both the journey home and the return to God
alternatives: turn me, and I will turn (repentance only)
decisions.reason: The verb is the same one used for repentance and for coming home from exile. Ephraim asks God to make him turn and confesses that he cannot turn on his own (compare Lamentations 5:21).

decisions.choice: Quotation marks for Ephraim's words
decisions.reason: Ephraim's prayer is speech quoted inside God's oracle, so it takes double quotation marks, opening here and closing at the end of verse 19. Its opening "You" begins a sentence and is capitalized at every setting.

decisions.choice: come back to you
decisions.reason: Readable adds "to you" to make plain that the return is to God.

decisions.choice: Hazme volver, y volveré
decisions.reason: *Shuv* twice (meaning decision m3): Spanish keeps "volver" for both the journey home and the turning back to God, as the terms note sets.

decisions.choice: unirudishe, nami nitarudi
decisions.reason: The same verb *shuv* twice, "kurudisha" and "kurudi", at every level, so Ephraim's turning back to God and God bringing him back are one word, as the terms note sets.

decisions.choice: "fais-moi revenir, et je reviendrai"
decisions.reason: Shuv as the terms note sets it for Jeremiah: "revenir" at every level, so the play between the journey home and the return to God stays (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: Ephraim prays as "con" and calls God "Ngài"; "trở lại" for both sides of shuv
decisions.reason: Ephraim's words are a prayer, so they take the prayer address of the terms note. "Đem con trở lại ... con sẽ trở lại" keeps one verb for God's bringing back and the people's turning, as meaning decision m3 explains.

decisions.choice: God's words in the plain style; Ephraim's prayer in 합쇼체 with "저" and "주님"
decisions.reason: God reports Ephraim's prayer (meaning decision m1), which runs to the end of verse 19; it is a prayer, so it takes the terms note's prayer style.

decisions.choice: "돌이켜 주십시오 ... 돌아가겠습니다" (L); "돌아가게 해 주십시오 ... 돌아가겠습니다" (B, R)
decisions.reason: *shuv* is "돌아오다/돌아가다" in Jeremiah, both the journey home and the return to God (meaning decision m3); "회개하다" stays for the Greek.

decisions.choice: tu (Ephraim to God); faze-me voltar ... voltarei
decisions.reason: Ephraim prays to God with "tu", as people speak to God through the Old Testament; his opening "Tu" begins a sentence and is written plainly. The same verb returns twice (m3), so each level repeats "voltar", the verb of coming home and of turning back to God.

source.text: כִּֽי־אַחֲרֵ֤י שׁוּבִי֙ נִחַ֔מְתִּי וְאַֽחֲרֵי֙ הִוָּ֣דְעִ֔י סָפַ֖קְתִּי עַל־יָרֵ֑ךְ בֹּ֚שְׁתִּי וְגַם־נִכְלַ֔מְתִּי כִּ֥י נָשָׂ֖אתִי חֶרְפַּ֥ת נְעוּרָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: For after my turning away I repented, and after I was made to know, I struck on [my] thigh; I was ashamed and also humiliated, because I bore [the] disgrace of my youth.

en.L: For after my turning away I repented, \q and after I was made to understand I struck [my] thigh; \q I was ashamed and also humiliated, \q for I bore the disgrace of my youth."
en.B: After I turned away, I was sorry; \q after I came to understand, I struck my thigh in grief. \q I was ashamed and disgraced, \q because I carried the shame of my youth."
en.R: After I turned away from {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, I was sorry. \q When I understood what I had done, I struck my thigh in grief. \q I was ashamed and felt disgraced, \q because I still carried the disgrace of the sins I did when I was young."

es.L: Porque después de apartarme, me arrepentí, \q y después de que se me hizo entender, me golpeé el muslo; \q me avergoncé y también me humillé, \q porque llevé la afrenta de mi juventud».
es.B: Después de apartarme, me arrepentí; \q después de comprender, me golpeé el muslo de dolor. \q Me avergoncé y quedé humillado, \q porque cargaba con la deshonra de mi juventud».
es.R: Después de que me aparté de {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}, me arrepentí. \q Cuando comprendí lo que había hecho, me golpeé el muslo de dolor. \q Me sentí avergonzado y humillado, \q porque todavía cargaba con la deshonra de los pecados que cometí cuando era joven».

fr.L: Car après m’être détourné, je me suis repenti, \q et après avoir été instruit, je me suis frappé [la] cuisse ; \q j’ai été honteux et même confus, \q car je portais l’opprobre de ma jeunesse. »
fr.B: Après m’être détourné, j’ai regretté ; \q après avoir compris, je me suis frappé la cuisse de douleur. \q J’ai été honteux et couvert de confusion, \q car je portais la honte de ma jeunesse. »
fr.R: Après m’être détourné de {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, j’ai regretté. \q Quand j’ai compris ce que j’avais fait, je me suis frappé la cuisse de douleur. \q J’avais honte et je me sentais déshonoré, \q parce que je portais encore la honte des péchés de ma jeunesse. »

sw.L: Kwa maana baada ya kugeuka kwangu nilitubu, \q na baada ya kufundishwa nilijipiga paja; \q niliaibika, naam, nikafedheheka, \q kwa sababu nilibeba aibu ya ujana wangu."
sw.B: Baada ya kugeuka mbali nilijuta; \q baada ya kuelewa, nilijipiga paja kwa huzuni. \q Niliona aibu na kufedheheka, \q kwa sababu nilibeba aibu ya ujana wangu."
sw.R: Baada ya kukuacha {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}, nilijuta. \q Nilipoelewa nilichokifanya, nilijipiga paja kwa huzuni. \q Niliona aibu na kujisikia nimedhalilika, \q kwa sababu bado nilibeba aibu ya dhambi nilizotenda nilipokuwa kijana."

vi.L: Vì sau khi con quay đi, con đã ăn năn, \q và sau khi con được cho hiểu, con đã đấm vào đùi; \q con hổ thẹn và cũng nhục nhã, \q vì con mang sự sỉ nhục của tuổi trẻ con."
vi.B: Sau khi lìa bỏ Ngài, con đã hối hận; \q sau khi hiểu ra, con đã đấm vào đùi mình mà đau buồn. \q Con hổ thẹn và nhục nhã, \q vì con mang nỗi xấu hổ của tuổi trẻ con."
vi.R: Sau khi lìa bỏ Ngài, con đã hối hận. \q Khi hiểu ra điều mình đã làm, con đã đấm vào đùi mình mà đau buồn. \q Con xấu hổ và cảm thấy nhục nhã, \q vì con vẫn mang nỗi nhục về những tội lỗi con đã phạm thuở còn trẻ."

ko.L: 제가 돌아선 뒤에 뉘우쳤고, \q 깨달은 뒤에 [제] 허벅지를 쳤습니다. \q 제가 부끄럽고 또 수치스러웠습니다. \q 제 젊은 시절의 치욕을 짊어졌기 때문입니다."
ko.B: 저는 주님에게서 돌아선 뒤에 뉘우쳤고, \q 깨닫고 나서는 슬퍼서 허벅지를 쳤습니다. \q 저는 부끄럽고 수치스러웠습니다. \q 젊은 시절에 지은 죄의 치욕을 짊어지고 있었기 때문입니다."
ko.R: 저는 주님에게서 돌아선 뒤에 후회했습니다. \q 제가 한 일을 깨닫고는 슬퍼서 허벅지를 쳤습니다. \q 저는 부끄럽고 창피했습니다. \q 젊었을 때 지은 죄의 수치를 아직도 짊어지고 있었기 때문입니다."

pt.L: Pois depois do meu desvio eu me arrependi, \q e depois que fui levado a entender, bati [na minha] coxa; \q fiquei envergonhado e também humilhado, \q pois carreguei a desonra da minha juventude."
pt.B: Depois que me desviei, eu me arrependi; \q depois que entendi, bati na coxa em sinal de dor. \q Fiquei envergonhado e humilhado, \q porque carreguei a vergonha da minha juventude."
pt.R: Depois que me afastei de {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}, eu me arrependi. \q Quando entendi o que tinha feito, bati na coxa de tanta dor. \q Fiquei com vergonha e me senti humilhado, \q porque ainda carregava a desonra dos pecados que cometi quando era jovem."

decisions.choice: after my turning away: after Ephraim turned from God
alternatives: after I turned back, I repented
decisions.reason: The word "turning" can mean turning away from God or turning back to him. With "I repented" following, it most likely means that after Ephraim had turned away, it came to regret it. Others read "after I turned back (to you), I repented", that is, sorrow followed the return.

decisions.choice: struck my thigh: a gesture of grief and dismay
decisions.reason: Slapping the thigh showed great sorrow or alarm (Ezekiel 21:17).

decisions.choice: the disgrace of my youth: the shame of the sins of Israel's early days
decisions.reason: The northern kingdom's "youth" is its early history, when it turned to other gods (3:24-25; compare Psalm 25:7). Ephraim feels the shame of that past.

decisions.choice: in grief
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the gesture meant.

decisions.choice: from you ... the sins I did when I was young
decisions.reason: Readable says from whom Ephraim turned and explains the disgrace of youth. Ephraim's words close here.

decisions.choice: me arrepentí
decisions.reason: The verb here is *nicham*, not *shuv*: Ephraim's sorrow over his sin, for which "arrepentirse" is the natural Spanish word, while *shuv* in verse 18 stays "volver".

decisions.choice: "뉘우치다" for *nicham* here
decisions.reason: Ephraim's sorrow after turning away (meaning decision m1); "뉘우치다" says regret without the Greek-based church word.

source.text: הֲבֵן֩ יַקִּ֨יר לִ֜י אֶפְרַ֗יִם אִ֚ם יֶ֣לֶד שַׁעֲשֻׁעִ֔ים כִּֽי־מִדֵּ֤י דַבְּרִי֙ בּ֔וֹ זָכֹ֥ר אֶזְכְּרֶ֖נּוּ ע֑וֹד עַל־כֵּ֗ן הָמ֤וּ מֵעַי֙ ל֔וֹ רַחֵ֥ם אֲֽרַחֲמֶ֖נּוּ נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: [Is] a son dear to me Ephraim, or a child of delights? For as often as I speak against him, I surely remember him still; therefore my inner parts are stirred for him; I will surely have compassion on him, declares Yahweh.

en.L: Is Ephraim a dear son to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, or a child of delight? \q For as often as I speak against him, \q I surely remember him still; \q therefore {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} inner parts are stirred for him; \q I will surely have compassion on him, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Is Ephraim {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} dear son, a child who delights {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}? \q For whenever I speak against him, \q I still remember him and cannot forget. \q That is why {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} heart aches for him; \q I will surely show him compassion, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Is Ephraim not {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} dear son, the child I love? \q Even when I speak against him, \q I still think of him. \q That is why {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} heart longs for him. \q I will surely show him mercy, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: ¿Es Efraín para {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} un hijo querido, o un niño en quien me deleito? \q Porque cada vez que hablo contra él, \q todavía me acuerdo de él; \q por eso {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} entrañas se conmueven por él; \q ciertamente tendré compasión de él, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.B: ¿Es Efraín {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} hijo querido, un niño que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} deleita? \q Porque siempre que hablo contra él, \q todavía lo recuerdo y no puedo olvidarlo. \q Por eso {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} corazón sufre por él; \q de cierto le mostraré compasión, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.R: ¿No es Efraín {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} hijo querido, el niño que amo? \q Aun cuando hablo contra él, \q sigo pensando en él. \q Por eso {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} corazón lo anhela. \q De cierto le mostraré misericordia, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.

fr.L: Éphraïm est-il pour {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} un fils chéri, ou un enfant de délices ? \q Car chaque fois que je parle contre lui, \q je {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} souviens encore de lui ; \q c’est pourquoi {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} entrailles s’émeuvent pour lui ; \q j’aurai certainement compassion de lui, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Éphraïm est-il {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} fils chéri, un enfant qui fait {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} délices ? \q Car chaque fois que je parle contre lui, \q je pense encore à lui et je ne peux l’oublier. \q C’est pourquoi {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} cœur se serre pour lui ; \q j’aurai vraiment compassion de lui, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Éphraïm n’est-il pas {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} fils chéri, l’enfant que j’aime ? \q Même quand je parle contre lui, \q je pense encore à lui. \q C’est pourquoi {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} cœur se languit de lui. \q J’aurai vraiment pitié de lui, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.

sw.L: Je, Efraimu ni mwana mpendwa {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}, au mtoto wa furaha? \q Kwa maana kila mara ninaposema juu yake, \q hakika ningali ninamkumbuka; \q kwa hiyo matumbo {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} yanataabika kwa ajili yake; \q hakika nitamhurumia, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Je, Efraimu ni mwanangu mpendwa, mtoto anayenifurahisha? \q Kwa maana kila ninaposema dhidi yake, \q bado ninamkumbuka wala siwezi kumsahau. \q Ndiyo maana moyo {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} unamwonea uchungu; \q hakika nitamwonea huruma, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Je, Efraimu si mwanangu mpendwa, mtoto ninayempenda? \q Hata ninaposema dhidi yake, \q bado ninamfikiria. \q Ndiyo maana moyo {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} unamtamani. \q Hakika nitamhurumia, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

vi.L: Ép-ra-im có phải là con yêu dấu của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, là đứa con làm {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} vui thích chăng? \q Vì mỗi lần {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} phán nghịch cùng nó, \q Ta vẫn nhớ đến nó; \q vì vậy lòng dạ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} xao xuyến vì nó; \q Ta chắc chắn sẽ thương xót nó, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy.
vi.B: Ép-ra-im có phải là con yêu dấu của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, đứa con làm {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} vui thích chăng? \q Vì mỗi khi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} phán nghịch cùng nó, \q Ta vẫn nhớ đến nó và không thể quên. \q Vì thế lòng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} quặn đau vì nó; \q Ta chắc chắn sẽ thương xót nó, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy.
vi.R: Ép-ra-im chẳng phải là con yêu dấu của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, là đứa con {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} thương yêu sao? \q Ngay cả khi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} phán nghịch cùng nó, \q Ta vẫn nghĩ đến nó. \q Vì thế lòng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} khao khát nó. \q Ta chắc chắn sẽ thương xót nó, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán.

ko.L: 에브라임은 나에게 귀한 아들, 기쁨이 되는 자식이 아니냐? \q 내가 그를 거슬러 말할 때마다 \q 나는 여전히 그를 기억한다. \q 그러므로 내 속이 그를 위하여 들끓는다. \q 내가 반드시 그를 불쌍히 여기겠다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 선언이다.
ko.B: 에브라임은 내가 아끼는 아들, 나를 기쁘게 하는 자식이 아니냐? \q 내가 그를 꾸짖을 때마다 \q 나는 여전히 그를 잊지 못한다. \q 그래서 내 마음이 그를 생각하며 아프다. \q 내가 반드시 그를 불쌍히 여기겠다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.
ko.R: 에브라임은 내가 아끼는 아들, 내가 사랑하는 자식이 아니냐? \q 내가 그를 꾸짖을 때에도 \q 나는 여전히 그를 생각한다. \q 그래서 내 마음은 그를 그리워한다. \q 내가 반드시 그에게 자비를 베풀겠다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.

pt.L: É Efraim um filho querido para {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}, ou uma criança das [minhas] delícias? \q Pois, sempre que falo contra ele, \q eu certamente ainda me lembro dele; \q por isso as {{deity_pronoun:minhas|Minhas}} entranhas se comovem por ele; \q eu certamente terei compaixão dele, declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}.
pt.B: Não é Efraim o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} filho querido, uma criança que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} alegra? \q Pois, sempre que falo contra ele, \q ainda me lembro dele e não consigo esquecê-lo. \q Por isso o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} coração sofre por ele; \q eu certamente terei compaixão dele, declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}.
pt.R: Não é Efraim o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} filho querido, a criança que eu amo? \q Mesmo quando falo contra ele, \q ainda penso nele. \q Por isso o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} coração deseja tanto estar com ele. \q Eu certamente vou ter misericórdia dele, diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}.

decisions.choice: Is Ephraim a dear son to me?: a question expecting the answer yes
alternatives: a question of wonder or surprise
decisions.reason: God answers Ephraim's prayer with a question that confesses his love: Ephraim is his precious child. Some read it as a question of wonder ("Is Ephraim really so dear to me, that ...?"), but the rest of the verse shows that the answer is yes.

decisions.choice: as often as I speak against him, I still remember him: even God's words of judgment do not end his love
decisions.reason: God has spoken against Ephraim many times through the prophets, yet the doubled verb stresses that he keeps remembering him with care.

decisions.choice: my inner parts are stirred: I am deeply moved
decisions.reason: The inner parts (the belly or bowels) were thought of as the seat of strong feeling (Isaiah 16:11; 63:15). The verb means to be in turmoil, to groan.

decisions.choice: have compassion: a love like a mother's for her child
decisions.reason: The verb is related to the word for womb. It echoes Rachel weeping for her children (verse 15): God's love for Ephraim is like a mother's.

decisions.choice: my heart (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use "heart" for the inner parts, where English places such feelings.

decisions.choice: Is Ephraim not my dear son
decisions.reason: Readable adds "not" to show that the question expects the answer yes.

decisions.choice: "lòng dạ Ta xao xuyến" for "my inner parts are stirred"
decisions.reason: Vietnamese "lòng dạ" is the inner self as the seat of feeling, which is what the Hebrew "inner parts" means; "ruột gan" would sound coarse.

decisions.choice: "내 속이 들끓다" (L); "내 마음이 아프다" (B); "내 마음이 그리워하다" (R)
decisions.reason: The inner parts as the seat of feeling (meaning decision m3); Literal keeps a bodily picture with "속", and Balanced and Readable say "마음", as the English says "heart".

decisions.choice: Não é Efraim ... ? (B)
alternatives: É Efraim o meu filho querido?
decisions.reason: A Portuguese question that expects "yes" (m1) is asked with "Não é ...?"; a bare "É Efraim ...?" would sound like real doubt. Literal keeps the Hebrew's plain question; Balanced and Readable add "Não", as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: as minhas entranhas se comovem (L); o meu coração (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew's inner parts (m3) with "entranhas", the Portuguese word that also carries deep feeling; Balanced and Readable say "coração", as the English does.

source.text: הַצִּ֧יבִי לָ֣ךְ צִיֻּנִ֗ים שִׂ֤מִי לָךְ֙ תַּמְרוּרִ֔ים שִׁ֣תִי לִבֵּ֔ךְ לַֽמְסִלָּ֖ה דֶּ֣רֶךְ הָלָ֑כְתְּ שׁ֚וּבִי בְּתוּלַ֣ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל שֻׁ֖בִי אֶל־עָרַ֥יִךְ אֵֽלֶּה׃

records.literal_gloss: Set up for yourself road markers, place for yourself guideposts; set your heart to the highway, [the] way [that] you went; return, virgin of Israel, return to these your cities.

en.L: Set up road markers for yourself; \q make guideposts for yourself; \q set your heart toward the highway, the road [by which] you went. \q Return, virgin Israel; \q return to these your cities.
en.B: Set up road markers for yourself; \q put up signposts. \q Fix your mind on the highway, the road you traveled. \q Come back, Virgin Israel; \q come back to these towns of yours.
en.R: Put up signs along the road. \q Set up markers to show the way. \q Remember the road you took when you went away. \q Come back, people of Israel, pure as a young woman. \q Come back to these towns of yours.

es.L: Ponte señales en el camino; \q colócate postes indicadores; \q fija tu corazón en la calzada, el camino [por donde] fuiste. \q Vuelve, virgen Israel; \q vuelve a estas tus ciudades.
es.B: Pon señales en el camino; \q levanta postes indicadores. \q Fíjate bien en la calzada, el camino por donde anduviste. \q Vuelve, virgen Israel; \q vuelve a estas ciudades tuyas.
es.R: Pon señales a lo largo del camino. \q Coloca marcas que indiquen la ruta. \q Recuerda el camino que tomaste cuando te fuiste. \q Vuelve, pueblo de Israel, pura como una joven. \q Vuelve a estas ciudades tuyas.

fr.L: Dresse pour toi des bornes, \q place pour toi des poteaux ; \q applique ton cœur à la route, au chemin [par lequel] tu es allée. \q Reviens, vierge d’Israël, \q reviens dans ces villes qui sont les tiennes.
fr.B: Plante des bornes sur ta route, \q dresse des poteaux indicateurs. \q Fixe ton attention sur la grand-route, le chemin que tu as suivi. \q Reviens, vierge Israël, \q reviens dans tes villes que voici.
fr.R: Mets des panneaux le long de la route. \q Place des repères pour montrer le chemin. \q Souviens-toi de la route que tu as prise en partant. \q Reviens, peuple d’Israël, toi qui es comme une jeune fille pure. \q Reviens dans tes villes.

sw.L: Jiwekee alama za njia; \q jifanyie nguzo za kuonyesha njia; \q uelekeze moyo wako kwenye barabara kuu, njia [uliyoipitia] ulipokwenda. \q Rudi, ee bikira Israeli; \q rudi kwenye miji yako hii.
sw.B: Jiwekee alama za njiani; \q simika vibao vya kuonyesha njia. \q Elekeza akili yako kwenye barabara kuu, njia uliyoipitia. \q Rudi, ee Bikira Israeli; \q rudi kwenye miji yako hii.
sw.R: Wekeni alama kando ya barabara. \q Simikeni vibao vya kuonyesha njia. \q Kumbukeni njia mliyoipitia mlipokwenda. \q Rudini, enyi watu wa Israeli, mlio safi kama msichana. \q Rudini kwenye miji yenu hii.

vi.L: Hãy dựng cho mình những cột mốc; \q hãy đặt cho mình những bảng chỉ đường; \q hãy để lòng ngươi hướng về đường cái, là con đường ngươi đã đi. \q Hãy trở về, hỡi trinh nữ Y-sơ-ra-ên; \q hãy trở về các thành này của ngươi.
vi.B: Hãy dựng cho mình những cột mốc; \q hãy đặt những bảng chỉ đường. \q Hãy ghi nhớ đường cái, là con đường con đã đi qua. \q Hãy trở về, hỡi Trinh Nữ Y-sơ-ra-ên; \q hãy trở về các thành này của con.
vi.R: Hãy cắm những tấm bảng dọc đường. \q Hãy dựng những cột mốc chỉ lối. \q Hãy nhớ con đường con đã đi khi rời quê hương. \q Hãy trở về, hỡi dân Y-sơ-ra-ên, trong trắng như một thiếu nữ. \q Hãy trở về các thành này của con.

ko.L: 너를 위하여 길표를 세우고, \q 너를 위하여 이정표를 두어라. \q 네가 갔던 길, 큰길에 네 마음을 두어라. \q 처녀 이스라엘아, 돌아오너라. \q 이 너의 성읍들로 돌아오너라.
ko.B: 길에 표지를 세우고, \q 이정표를 세워라. \q 네가 걸어간 길, 그 큰길을 잘 기억해 두어라. \q 처녀 이스라엘아, 돌아오너라. \q 너의 이 성읍들로 돌아오너라.
ko.R: 길을 따라 표지판을 세워라. \q 길을 알려 주는 표시를 세워라. \q 네가 떠나갈 때 걸었던 길을 기억하여라. \q 깨끗한 처녀 같은 이스라엘 백성아, 돌아오너라. \q 너의 이 성읍들로 돌아오너라.

pt.L: Levanta para ti marcos de estrada; \q põe para ti postes de sinalização; \q põe o teu coração na estrada, o caminho [pelo qual] foste. \q Volta, virgem Israel; \q volta para estas tuas cidades.
pt.B: Levanta marcos na estrada; \q coloca placas de sinalização. \q Presta atenção na estrada, no caminho por onde andaste. \q Volta, virgem Israel; \q volta para estas cidades que são tuas.
pt.R: Coloca placas ao longo da estrada. \q Põe marcos para mostrar o caminho. \q Lembra-te da estrada que seguiste quando foste embora. \q Volta, povo de Israel, pura como uma moça. \q Volta para estas cidades que são tuas.

decisions.choice: you went: the reading the scribes marked to be read aloud
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew letters can be read "I went"; the scribes' marginal note (qere) reads "you went", which suits the woman addressed throughout the verse. The translation follows the marginal reading.

decisions.choice: road markers, guideposts: stones or posts set up to mark the way
decisions.reason: The exiles are to mark the road as they leave, so that they can find it again on the way home. The word for guideposts sounds the same as "bitter" in verse 15: the road of bitter tears becomes the road home.

decisions.choice: set your heart: pay close attention, keep in mind
decisions.reason: The heart is the seat of thought and will.

decisions.choice: Come back (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The verb that means both turning back to God and coming home is "return" at Literal and "come back" at Balanced and Readable, as in verse 18.

decisions.choice: "trở về" (come back home)
decisions.reason: Here shuv is the homecoming from exile, so it takes "trở về", as the terms note gives for return from exile; "quay về" is kept for repentance.

decisions.choice: Volta (every level)
decisions.reason: The verb of turning back to God and of coming home is "voltar" at every level, as in verse 18; Portuguese "voltar" has both senses, so the levels need not differ as the English "return" / "come back" do.

source.text: עַד־מָתַי֙ תִּתְחַמָּקִ֔ין הַבַּ֖ת הַשּֽׁוֹבֵבָ֑ה כִּֽי־בָרָ֨א יְהוָ֤ה חֲדָשָׁה֙ בָּאָ֔רֶץ נְקֵבָ֖ה תְּס֥וֹבֵֽב גָּֽבֶר׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Until when will you turn this way and that, the daughter, the faithless one? For Yahweh has created a new [thing] in the land: a female will surround a man.

en.L: How long will you turn this way and that, \q faithless daughter? \q For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has created a new thing in the land: \q a female will surround a man.
en.B: How long will you waver this way and that, \q you faithless daughter? \q For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has created something new in the land: \q a woman will encircle a man.
en.R: How long will you keep wandering here and there, \q you unfaithful daughter? \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has made something new happen in the land: \q a woman will surround a man.

es.L: ¿Hasta cuándo andarás de aquí para allá, \q hija infiel? \q Porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha creado algo nuevo en la tierra: \q la mujer rodeará al varón.
es.B: ¿Hasta cuándo vacilarás de un lado a otro, \q hija infiel? \q Porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha creado algo nuevo en la tierra: \q una mujer rodeará a un hombre.
es.R: ¿Hasta cuándo seguirás andando de un lado a otro, \q hija infiel? \q {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha hecho que suceda algo nuevo en la tierra: \q una mujer rodeará a un hombre.

fr.L: Jusqu’à quand iras-tu çà et là, \q fille infidèle ? \q Car {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} crée une chose nouvelle sur la terre : \q la femme entourera l’homme.
fr.B: Jusqu’à quand hésiteras-tu de-ci de-là, \q fille infidèle ? \q Car {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} crée du nouveau dans le pays : \q une femme entoure un homme.
fr.R: Combien de temps vas-tu encore errer de tous côtés, \q fille infidèle ? \q {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} fait arriver quelque chose de nouveau dans le pays : \q une femme entourera un homme.

sw.L: Hata lini utageuka huku na huku, \q ewe binti asiye mwaminifu? \q Kwa maana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ameumba jambo jipya katika nchi: \q mwanamke atamzunguka mwanamume.
sw.B: Hata lini utasitasita huku na huku, \q ewe binti usiye mwaminifu? \q Kwa maana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ameumba jambo jipya katika nchi: \q mwanamke atamzingira mwanamume.
sw.R: Mtaendelea mpaka lini kutangatanga huku na huku, \q enyi mlio kama binti asiye mwaminifu? \q {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amefanya jambo jipya litokee katika nchi: \q mwanamke atamzunguka mwanamume.

vi.L: Hỡi con gái bất trung kia, \q ngươi còn lưỡng lự cho đến bao giờ? \q Vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã tạo nên một điều mới trên đất: \q người nữ sẽ bao quanh người nam.
vi.B: Hỡi con gái bất trung kia, \q con còn do dự chần chừ cho đến bao giờ? \q Vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã tạo nên một điều mới trên đất: \q người nữ sẽ ôm lấy người nam.
vi.R: Hỡi con gái bất trung kia, \q con còn đi lang thang chỗ này chỗ nọ cho đến bao giờ? \q {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã làm một điều mới xảy ra trên đất: \q người nữ sẽ bao bọc người nam.

ko.L: 언제까지 이리저리 헤매겠느냐, \q 믿음을 저버린 딸아? \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이 땅에 새 일을 창조하셨다. \q 여자가 남자를 둘러쌀 것이다.
ko.B: 언제까지 이리저리 망설이겠느냐, \q 믿음을 저버린 딸아? \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이 땅에 새로운 일을 창조하셨다. \q 여자가 남자를 감싸 안을 것이다.
ko.R: 언제까지 이리저리 헤매고 다니겠느냐, \q 믿음 없는 딸아? \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이 땅에 새로운 일을 일으키셨다. \q 여자가 남자를 둘러쌀 것이다.

pt.L: Até quando andarás de um lado para outro, \q filha infiel? \q Pois {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} criou uma coisa nova na terra: \q uma mulher rodeará um homem.
pt.B: Até quando hesitarás para cá e para lá, \q filha infiel? \q Pois {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} criou algo novo na terra: \q uma mulher envolverá um homem.
pt.R: Até quando vais ficar andando de um lado para outro, \q filha infiel? \q {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} fez acontecer uma coisa nova na terra: \q uma mulher vai rodear um homem.

decisions.choice: turn this way and that, faithless daughter: Israel hesitating to come home
decisions.reason: The verb means to turn about, to waver. "Faithless" comes from the same root as "return" in verse 21, a play on words heard also in 3:14, 22: the daughter who turns away is called to turn back.

decisions.choice: the LORD has created a new thing: something only God can bring about
decisions.reason: The verb for create is used only of God (Genesis 1:1; Isaiah 43:19; 65:17). The new thing gives the hesitant daughter a reason to come home.

decisions.choice: a female will surround a man: a saying whose meaning is very uncertain
alternatives: a woman will protect a man
a woman will court (or embrace) a man
decisions.reason: The words are clear, but their sense is not. Readings offered include: the woman (Israel) will embrace or seek her husband (God), reversing her running away; the weak will protect the strong, as a woman guarding a warrior, so that Israel will be safe; or a woman will court a man, a sign of a world turned upside down by joy. Some early Christian readers saw in it the virgin birth. The text itself does not settle it, and the translation keeps the bare words.

decisions.choice: in the land: in Israel's own land, or on the earth
decisions.reason: The word can mean the earth or the land. The call to return to "these your cities" (verse 21) favors the land of Israel.

decisions.choice: you unfaithful daughter
decisions.reason: Readable says "unfaithful" for faithless, a more common word.

decisions.choice: la mujer rodeará al varón / una mujer rodeará a un hombre
decisions.reason: The saying is very uncertain (meaning decision m3), so every level keeps the plain words "rodear" and "mujer ... hombre" rather than choosing one explanation.

decisions.choice: "la femme entourera l'homme" (L); "une femme entoure un homme" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the English: the saying is very uncertain (meaning decision m3), so every level keeps the plain verb "entourer" and does not choose one explanation.

decisions.choice: "người nữ sẽ bao quanh / ôm lấy / bao bọc người nam"
decisions.reason: The saying is very uncertain (meaning decision m3), so each level keeps close to the Hebrew picture and does not choose one explanation; Balanced's "ôm lấy" (embrace) follows the English "encircle".

decisions.choice: "여자가 남자를 둘러쌀 것이다" (L, R); "감싸 안을 것이다" (B)
decisions.reason: The saying is very uncertain (meaning decision m3); Korean keeps the bare words, as the English does, without choosing one explanation.

decisions.choice: "믿음을 저버린 딸" (L, B); "믿음 없는 딸" (R)
decisions.reason: The terms note's wording for *meshuvah*, faithless Israel, "믿음을 저버린".

decisions.choice: uma mulher rodeará / envolverá um homem
alternatives: uma mulher buscará o seu marido
decisions.reason: The meaning of the saying is very uncertain (m3), so every level keeps its words, as the English does, without choosing one reading: "rodear" and "envolver" can describe an embrace or a protecting circle.

source.text: כֹּֽה־אָמַ֞ר יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל ע֣וֹד יֹאמְר֞וּ אֶת־הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֗ה בְּאֶ֤רֶץ יְהוּדָה֙ וּבְעָרָ֔יו בְּשׁוּבִ֖י אֶת־שְׁבוּתָ֑ם יְבָרֶכְךָ֧ יְהוָ֛ה נְוֵה־צֶ֖דֶק הַ֥ר הַקֹּֽדֶשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus says Yahweh of hosts, [the] God of Israel: Again they will say the word the this in [the] land of Judah and in its cities, when I restore their fortunes: May Yahweh bless you, abode of righteousness, mountain of holiness.

en.L: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, the God of Israel: Once again they will say this word in the land of Judah and in its cities, when I restore their fortunes: "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} bless you, abode of righteousness, mountain of holiness."
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the God of Israel, says this: When I restore their fortunes, people in the land of Judah and in its towns will once again use these words: "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} bless you, home of righteousness, holy mountain!"
en.R: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the God of Israel, says: When I make things good again for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, those who live in the land of Judah and its towns will say once more, "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} bless you, holy mountain, home where righteousness lives!"

es.L: Así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos, el Dios de Israel: Otra vez dirán esta palabra en la tierra de Judá y en sus ciudades, cuando yo restaure su suerte: «{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} te bendiga, morada de justicia, monte de santidad».
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos, el Dios de Israel, dice esto: Cuando yo restaure su suerte, la gente de la tierra de Judá y de sus ciudades volverá a decir estas palabras: «¡Que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} te bendiga, morada de justicia, monte santo!».
es.R: Esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos, el Dios de Israel: Cuando yo haga que todo vuelva a ir bien para {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo, los que viven en la tierra de Judá y en sus ciudades dirán otra vez: «¡Que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} te bendiga, monte santo, hogar donde vive la justicia!».

fr.L: Ainsi parle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, le Dieu d’Israël : On dira encore cette parole dans le pays de Juda et dans ses villes, quand je rétablirai leur sort : « Que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} te bénisse, demeure de justice, montagne de sainteté ! »
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, le Dieu d’Israël, dit ceci : Quand je rétablirai leur sort, on dira de nouveau ces paroles dans le pays de Juda et dans ses villes : « Que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} te bénisse, demeure de la justice, montagne sainte ! »
fr.R: Voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées, le Dieu d’Israël : Quand je rendrai de nouveau heureux {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple, ceux qui habitent le pays de Juda et ses villes diront encore : « Que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} te bénisse, montagne sainte, maison où habite la justice ! »

sw.L: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, Mungu wa Israeli, asema hivi: Tena watasema neno hili katika nchi ya Yuda na katika miji yake, nitakapowarudishia mafanikio yao: "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akubariki, ee makao ya haki, ee mlima wa utakatifu."
sw.B: Hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, Mungu wa Israeli, asemavyo: Nitakapowarudishia mafanikio yao, watu katika nchi ya Yuda na katika miji yake watatumia tena maneno haya: "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akubariki, ee makao ya haki, ee mlima mtakatifu!"
sw.R: Hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi, Mungu wa Israeli, analosema: Nitakapoyafanya mambo kuwa mema tena kwa watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, wale wanaoishi katika nchi ya Yuda na miji yake watasema tena, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akubariki, ee mlima mtakatifu, makao ambamo haki inakaa!"

vi.L: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân, Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên, phán thế này: Khi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} phục hồi cơ đồ của chúng, người ta sẽ lại nói lời này trong xứ Giu-đa và trong các thành của nó: "Nguyện {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ban phước cho ngươi, hỡi nơi ở của sự công chính, hỡi núi thánh."
vi.B: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân, Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên, phán như vầy: Khi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} phục hồi cơ đồ của họ, người ta trong xứ Giu-đa và các thành của nó sẽ lại nói: "Nguyện {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ban phước cho ngươi, hỡi nơi ngự của sự công chính, hỡi núi thánh!"
vi.R: Đây là lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân, Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên, phán: Khi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} làm cho mọi sự tốt đẹp trở lại cho dân Ta, những người sống trong xứ Giu-đa và các thành của nó sẽ lại nói: "Nguyện {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ban phước cho ngươi, hỡi núi thánh, là nơi sự công chính ngự!"

ko.L: 이스라엘의 하나님 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이와 같이 말씀하신다. 내가 그들의 운명을 돌이킬 때에, 유다 땅과 그 성읍들에서 그들이 다시 이 말을 할 것이다. "의로운 처소, 거룩한 산이여, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 너에게 복을 주시기를 바란다."
ko.B: 이스라엘의 하나님 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이렇게 말씀하신다. 내가 그들의 형편을 회복시키면, 유다 땅과 그 성읍들에 사는 사람들이 다시 이렇게 말할 것이다. "의가 머무는 곳, 거룩한 산이여, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 너에게 복을 주시기를 바란다!"
ko.R: 이스라엘의 하나님, 하늘의 군대를 거느리신 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 하시는 말씀이다. 내가 내 백성을 다시 잘되게 해 주면, 유다 땅과 그 성읍들에 사는 사람들이 다시 이렇게 말할 것이다. "의가 사는 곳, 거룩한 산이여, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 너에게 복을 주시기를!"

pt.L: Assim diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos, o Deus de Israel: Outra vez dirão esta palavra na terra de Judá e nas suas cidades, quando eu restaurar a sorte deles: "{{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} te abençoe, morada da justiça, monte da santidade."
pt.B: Assim diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos, o Deus de Israel: Quando eu restaurar a sorte deles, o povo da terra de Judá e das suas cidades dirá outra vez estas palavras: "{{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} te abençoe, morada da justiça, monte santo!"
pt.R: É isto que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos, o Deus de Israel, diz: Quando eu fizer a vida do {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} povo voltar a ser boa, os que moram na terra de Judá e nas suas cidades vão dizer de novo: "{{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} te abençoe, monte santo, lugar onde mora a justiça!"

decisions.choice: restore their fortunes: bring the people back from exile and make them prosper
decisions.reason: The phrase means to turn things back to how they were, and in Jeremiah it often includes the return of the captives (29:14; 30:3, 18).

decisions.choice: abode of righteousness, mountain of holiness: Jerusalem and the temple mount
decisions.reason: The first word means a pasture or a settled home. The blessing is spoken over Zion, the holy hill where God lives (Psalm 2:6; Isaiah 1:26). In 50:7 the LORD himself is called the "abode of righteousness" of Israel's ancestors.

decisions.choice: prose from here to the end of the chapter
decisions.reason: From this verse on, the chapter is set as prose. Verses 23-26 still have parallel lines, and so do verses 35-37, but they are joined to the prose promises of verses 27-40 and set the same way.

decisions.choice: the LORD of hosts (Literal); the LORD of Armies (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in Isaiah.

decisions.choice: people ... those who live
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "they will say" has no named subject; Balanced and Readable supply one. Readable also explains "restore their fortunes".

decisions.choice: Verses 23-40 set as prose, without lines
decisions.reason: As the English: the chapter turns to prose here (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: restaurar a sorte deles (L, B)
alternatives: trazer de volta os seus cativos
decisions.reason: The phrase means turning things back to how they were (m1); "restaurar a sorte" says that and leaves room for the return of the exiles it often includes. Readable explains it with the words 30:3 sets, "fazer a vida ... voltar a ser boa", as the English Readable explains it. "O SENHOR dos Exércitos" is the title at every level, as Isaiah 1:9 sets it.

source.text: וְיָ֥שְׁבוּ בָ֛הּ יְהוּדָ֥ה וְכָל־עָרָ֖יו יַחְדָּ֑ו אִכָּרִ֕ים וְנָסְע֖וּ בַּעֵֽדֶר׃

records.literal_gloss: And will dwell in it Judah and all its cities together, farmers, and they journey with [the] flock.

en.L: And Judah and all its cities will dwell in it together, farmers and [those who] travel with the flock.
en.B: Judah and all its towns will live there together, the farmers and those who move about with the flocks.
en.R: The people of Judah and of all its towns will live there together. Farmers will live there, and so will shepherds who move from place to place with their sheep.

es.L: Y habitarán en ella Judá y todas sus ciudades juntamente, los labradores y los que andan con el rebaño.
es.B: Judá y todas sus ciudades vivirán allí juntos, los agricultores y los que se trasladan con los rebaños.
es.R: La gente de Judá y de todas sus ciudades vivirá allí junta. Allí vivirán los agricultores, y también los pastores que van de un lugar a otro con sus ovejas.

fr.L: Et Juda et toutes ses villes y habiteront ensemble, les cultivateurs et [ceux qui] se déplacent avec le troupeau.
fr.B: Juda et toutes ses villes y habiteront ensemble, les cultivateurs et ceux qui vont de lieu en lieu avec les troupeaux.
fr.R: Les gens de Juda et de toutes ses villes y habiteront ensemble. Les cultivateurs y habiteront, et aussi les bergers qui se déplacent d’un endroit à l’autre avec leurs moutons.

sw.L: Na Yuda na miji yake yote watakaa ndani yake pamoja, wakulima na [wale] wanaosafiri na kundi.
sw.B: Yuda na miji yake yote wataishi huko pamoja, wakulima na wale wanaohamahama na makundi yao.
sw.R: Watu wa Yuda na wa miji yake yote wataishi huko pamoja. Wakulima wataishi huko, na wachungaji wanaohama mahali hadi mahali pamoja na kondoo wao.

vi.L: Giu-đa cùng mọi thành của nó sẽ ở chung tại đó, những người làm ruộng và [những người] đi theo bầy gia súc.
vi.B: Giu-đa và mọi thành của nó sẽ cùng sống tại đó, cả những người làm ruộng lẫn những người dẫn bầy gia súc đi khắp nơi.
vi.R: Dân Giu-đa và dân mọi thành của nó sẽ cùng sống tại đó. Những người làm ruộng sẽ sống ở đó, và cả những người chăn chiên đi từ nơi này đến nơi khác với bầy chiên của mình.

ko.L: 그리고 유다와 그 모든 성읍이 그 안에서 함께 살 것이고, 농부들과 양 떼를 몰고 다니는 [자들도 그러할 것이다].
ko.B: 유다와 그 모든 성읍의 사람들이 그곳에서 함께 살 것이다. 농부들과 양 떼를 몰고 다니는 사람들도 함께 살 것이다.
ko.R: 유다와 그 모든 성읍의 사람들이 그곳에서 함께 살 것이다. 농부들도 거기에서 살 것이고, 양 떼를 몰고 이곳저곳 다니는 목자들도 살 것이다.

pt.L: E nela habitarão Judá e todas as suas cidades juntamente, lavradores e [os que] andam com o rebanho.
pt.B: Judá e todas as suas cidades morarão ali juntos, os lavradores e os que andam de um lugar a outro com os rebanhos.
pt.R: O povo de Judá e de todas as suas cidades vai morar ali junto. Ali vão morar os lavradores, e também os pastores que andam de um lugar para outro com as suas ovelhas.

decisions.choice: in it: in the land of Judah
decisions.reason: "It" refers back to the land of Judah of verse 23.

decisions.choice: farmers and those who travel with the flock: both settled and roaming ways of life
decisions.reason: Farmers stayed with their fields; shepherds moved from pasture to pasture. Both can live safely in the land again, with no enemy to fear (contrast 6:3; 33:12-13).

decisions.choice: shepherds who move from place to place
decisions.reason: Readable says who those traveling with the flocks are.

source.text: כִּ֥י הִרְוֵ֖יתִי נֶ֣פֶשׁ עֲיֵפָ֑ה וְכָל־נֶ֥פֶשׁ דָּאֲבָ֖ה מִלֵּֽאתִי׃

records.literal_gloss: For I give drink [to the] weary soul, and every languishing soul I fill.

en.L: For I give drink to the weary soul, and every languishing soul I fill.
en.B: For I refresh the weary soul and satisfy everyone who is faint.
en.R: I give new strength to those who are tired, and I satisfy all who are weak.

es.L: Porque yo doy de beber al alma cansada, y sacio a toda alma desfallecida.
es.B: Porque yo reanimo al alma cansada y sacio a todo el que desfallece.
es.R: Yo doy nuevas fuerzas a los que están cansados, y sacio a todos los que están débiles.

fr.L: Car je désaltère l’âme fatiguée, et je rassasie toute âme qui languit.
fr.B: Car je rafraîchis celui qui est épuisé et je rassasie tous ceux qui défaillent.
fr.R: Je redonne des forces à ceux qui sont fatigués, et je comble tous ceux qui sont faibles.

sw.L: Kwa maana ninainywesha nafsi iliyochoka, na kila nafsi iliyodhoofika ninaishibisha.
sw.B: Kwa maana ninaiburudisha nafsi iliyochoka na kumshibisha kila aliyezimia.
sw.R: Ninawapa nguvu mpya wale waliochoka, na ninawatosheleza wote walio dhaifu.

vi.L: Vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cho linh hồn mệt mỏi được uống, và mọi linh hồn héo hon {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} làm cho no đủ.
vi.B: Vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} làm tươi tỉnh linh hồn mệt mỏi và làm no đủ mọi người kiệt sức.
vi.R: Ta ban sức mới cho những người mệt mỏi, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} làm cho mọi người yếu đuối được no đủ.

ko.L: 내가 지친 영혼에게 마시게 하고, 시든 모든 영혼을 채우기 때문이다.
ko.B: 내가 지친 사람에게 새 힘을 주고, 기력이 다한 모든 사람을 배부르게 하기 때문이다.
ko.R: 나는 지친 사람들에게 새 힘을 주고, 약한 사람들을 모두 넉넉하게 채워 준다.

pt.L: Pois eu dou de beber à alma cansada, e toda alma que definha eu sacio.
pt.B: Pois eu reanimo a alma cansada e sacio todos os que desfalecem.
pt.R: Eu dou força nova aos que estão cansados e satisfaço todos os que estão fracos.

decisions.choice: I give drink ... I fill: God's settled purpose, spoken of as already done
alternatives: I have refreshed ... I have filled
decisions.reason: The verbs are in the past form, used here for what God has firmly decided to do. They pick up verses 12 and 14: the soul like a watered garden, the priests' soul filled.

decisions.choice: the weary soul, every languishing soul: people worn out by the suffering of war and exile
decisions.reason: "Soul" means the whole person, here as thirsty and faint. The word for languishing is the one in verse 12: "they will not languish again".

decisions.choice: give new strength
decisions.reason: Readable says what giving drink to the weary means.

source.text: עַל־זֹ֖את הֱקִיצֹ֣תִי וָאֶרְאֶ֑ה וּשְׁנָתִ֖י עָ֥רְבָה לִּֽי׃ס

records.literal_gloss: On this I awoke and looked, and my sleep was pleasant to me.

en.L: At this I awoke and looked, and my sleep was pleasant to me.
en.B: At this I woke up and looked around, and my sleep had been sweet to me.
en.R: Then I woke up and looked around. My sleep had been pleasant.

es.L: En esto me desperté y miré, y mi sueño me fue agradable.
es.B: En esto me desperté y miré a mi alrededor, y mi sueño me había sido dulce.
es.R: Entonces me desperté y miré a mi alrededor. Había dormido bien.

fr.L: Là-dessus je m’éveillai et je regardai, et mon sommeil m’avait été agréable.
fr.B: Là-dessus je me réveillai et regardai autour de moi, et mon sommeil avait été doux.
fr.R: Alors je me suis réveillé et j’ai regardé autour de moi. J’avais bien dormi.

sw.L: Juu ya hili niliamka na kutazama, na usingizi wangu ulikuwa mtamu kwangu.
sw.B: Hapo niliamka nikatazama huku na huku, na usingizi wangu ulikuwa umenipendeza.
sw.R: Kisha niliamka nikatazama huku na huku. Usingizi wangu ulikuwa mzuri.

vi.L: Đến đây tôi thức dậy và nhìn, và giấc ngủ của tôi thật êm dịu đối với tôi.
vi.B: Đến đây tôi tỉnh dậy và nhìn quanh, và giấc ngủ của tôi đã thật êm dịu.
vi.R: Rồi tôi thức dậy và nhìn quanh. Giấc ngủ của tôi thật dễ chịu.

ko.L: 이때에 내가 깨어 보니, 내 잠이 나에게 달았다.
ko.B: 이때에 내가 깨어나서 둘러보니, 내 잠이 달콤했다.
ko.R: 그때 나는 잠에서 깨어 둘러보았다. 나는 단잠을 잤다.

pt.L: Nisto eu despertei e olhei, e o meu sono me foi agradável.
pt.B: Nisto eu acordei e olhei ao redor, e o meu sono tinha sido doce para mim.
pt.R: Então eu acordei e olhei em volta. O meu sono tinha sido muito bom.

decisions.choice: I awoke: the prophet speaks, waking from a revelation given in sleep
decisions.reason: The speaker is most likely Jeremiah. The promises of verses 2-25 (or at least 23-25) came to him as in a dream, and he wakes refreshed by them. The verse is very unusual in Jeremiah, and some take it as the words of the exiles, or of God rising to act (Psalm 78:65).

decisions.choice: my sleep was pleasant: the vision gave peace
decisions.reason: Unlike troubling dreams (Daniel 2:1), this one left the sleeper glad.

decisions.choice: looked around
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "around" to make clear that the prophet, now awake, looks at what is about him.

decisions.choice: "je m'éveillai" (L, B); "je me suis réveillé" (R)
decisions.reason: The prophet tells of his own waking, a small piece of narrative: passé simple at Literal and Balanced, passé composé at Readable, as for Jeremiah's other first-person narrative.

decisions.choice: "내가" in the plain style
decisions.reason: The prophet speaks of himself, waking from a revelation given in sleep (meaning decision m1); he is not addressing God, so he says "나" in the plain style.

source.text: הִנֵּ֛ה יָמִ֥ים בָּאִ֖ים נְאֻם־יְהוָ֑ה וְזָרַעְתִּ֗י אֶת־בֵּ֤ית יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וְאֶת־בֵּ֣ית יְהוּדָ֔ה זֶ֥רַע אָדָ֖ם וְזֶ֥רַע בְּהֵמָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Look, days [are] coming, declares Yahweh, when I will sow [the] house of Israel and [the] house of Judah [with] seed of man and seed of beast.

en.L: Look, days are coming, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when I will sow the house of Israel and the house of Judah [with] seed of {{gender:humankind|man}} and seed of beast.
en.B: The days are coming, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when I will sow seed in the house of Israel and the house of Judah, the seed of people and the seed of animals.
en.R: A time is coming, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when I will fill Israel and Judah with people and animals, as a farmer sows a field with seed.

es.L: He aquí vienen días, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, en que sembraré la casa de Israel y la casa de Judá [con] simiente de hombre y simiente de animal.
es.B: Vienen días, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, en que sembraré la casa de Israel y la casa de Judá con semilla de personas y semilla de animales.
es.R: Se acerca el tiempo, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, en que llenaré Israel y Judá de gente y de animales, como un agricultor siembra un campo con semilla.

fr.L: Voici, des jours viennent, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, où j’ensemencerai la maison d’Israël et la maison de Juda d’une semence d’{{gender:humains|hommes}} et d’une semence de bêtes.
fr.B: Des jours viennent, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, où je sèmerai dans la maison d’Israël et dans la maison de Juda une semence de gens et une semence de bêtes.
fr.R: Un temps vient, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, où je remplirai Israël et Juda de gens et d’animaux, comme un cultivateur sème un champ.

sw.L: Tazama, siku zinakuja, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, nitakapoipanda nyumba ya Israeli na nyumba ya Yuda [kwa] mbegu ya wanadamu na mbegu ya wanyama.
sw.B: Siku zinakuja, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, nitakapopanda mbegu katika nyumba ya Israeli na nyumba ya Yuda, mbegu ya watu na mbegu ya wanyama.
sw.R: Wakati unakuja, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, nitakapoijaza Israeli na Yuda watu na wanyama, kama mkulima apandavyo mbegu shambani.

vi.L: Kìa, những ngày đang đến, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy, khi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ gieo vào nhà Y-sơ-ra-ên và nhà Giu-đa giống của loài người và giống của thú vật.
vi.B: Sẽ đến những ngày, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ gieo vào nhà Y-sơ-ra-ên và nhà Giu-đa giống của loài người và giống của thú vật.
vi.R: Sẽ đến lúc, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ làm cho Y-sơ-ra-ên và Giu-đa đầy dẫy người và thú vật, như người nông dân gieo hạt giống khắp cánh đồng.

ko.L: 보아라, 날들이 온다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 선언이다. 그때에 내가 이스라엘 집과 유다 집에 사람의 씨와 짐승의 씨를 뿌리겠다.
ko.B: 때가 오고 있다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다. 그때에 내가 이스라엘 집과 유다 집에 사람의 씨와 짐승의 씨를 뿌리겠다.
ko.R: 때가 오고 있다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다. 그때에 내가 농부가 밭에 씨를 뿌리듯이 이스라엘과 유다를 사람과 짐승으로 가득 채우겠다.

pt.L: Eis que vêm dias, declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, em que semearei a casa de Israel e a casa de Judá [com] semente de {{gender:gente|homem}} e semente de animal.
pt.B: Vêm dias, declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, em que semearei a casa de Israel e a casa de Judá com semente de gente e semente de animais.
pt.R: Está chegando o tempo, diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, em que vou encher Israel e Judá de gente e de animais, como um lavrador semeia um campo.

decisions.choice: sow with the seed of humans and of animals: fill the land again with people and livestock
